_comment: LUL-589: named markers that must still appear in each workflow file after any PR touching .github/workflows/*. Read from main's copy by .github/scripts/workflow-guard-check.sh -- never from the branch being checked, same rule ship-allowed.sh follows. A missing marker means a guard got silently deleted (PR #108: a stale branch's copy of auto-pr.yml had zero references to deployment-budget.sh). Widen this list whenever a new guard lands; do not narrow it without board sign-off.
_comment_bot_approve: LUL-826: the `statusCheckRollup` marker pins guard 2's SOURCE, not merely its presence. LUL-826 was filed proposing that guard 2 fall back to REST /commits/{sha}/check-runs whenever the rollup looks incomplete; measured on PR #166, that fallback would have approved a PR whose merge GitHub still refused with '3 of 3 required status checks are expected'. The rollup is the only view the merge engine agrees with. A future diff swapping this read for a REST one is the regression this marker exists to catch. ORDERING: bot-approve.yml is not on main yet (LUL-807). This entry only takes effect once MAIN's copy of this manifest carries it -- which is the same release-train cut that carries the workflow itself, since both live on release/next today. If bot-approve.yml is ever retired, remove this entry in the SAME commit or every branch's workflow-guard-check goes red on 'the file itself is gone'.
_comment_daily_report: LUL-925: `--base release/next` pins daily-report.yml's PR TARGET. It shipped opening its nightly PR with `--base main`, which base-branch-guard.sh fails by design (base `main` requires head `release/next` or an `emergency-hotfix` label), so every report PR opened structurally unmergeable and sat red -- PR #206, run 33156610173. Reverting that one flag is the regression this marker catches. ORDERING: same rule as bot-approve above -- this entry only bites once MAIN's copy of the manifest carries it, i.e. after the version cut that also carries the fixed workflow. Note version-cut.yml legitimately uses `--base main --head release/next`; it is the one path to main and is deliberately NOT covered here.
